## Small cards load models whose decoded copy does not fit (Arc A380); Inkling 2 with ~190 fewer launches a token

- **A model whose decoded weights do not fit the card is decoded just in time instead of failing to load** (#99): an Arc A380 (5.6 GiB) could not load the 4B, because the plan kept a decoded copy (7.3 GiB with the file) that the card cannot hold. The copy is now checked against the GPU's own memory; where it does not fit, the weights are decoded just in time (~3 GiB for the 4B), with a line saying so. Where it fits, nothing changes.
- **Memory tiers in `--ctx auto` for every model**: resident weights, then just in time, then part of the weights in host memory. A model is refused only when even the last leaves no context.
- **Launchers**: the Alchemist "best measured" resident setting for the 4B / 9B applies to an A770 only now; `./zero-launcher.sh` asks for 8 GB of RAM with a discrete card (it asked for 15).
- **Inkling 2 generates with about 190 fewer GPU launches a token** (#45): its attention projections run as one matrix a token, and the k / v inputs' norms with their quantization in one launch. A Pro B60: 1,548 -> 1,356 launches a token, the same numbers bit for bit.

**Please test on your card** (an A380 or any card that could not load a model before; paste the output into #99):

```
serverz -m Qwen3.5-4B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --ctx auto
runz Qwen3.5-4B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf "Explain in three short sentences why the sky is blue." --n 128 --show
```

Look for the line "the weights are decoded just in time" and the context `--ctx auto` picks.
